newsitem.title: USA: CBOT says filed Supreme Court brief on CEA changes.
newsitem.headline: CBOT says filed Supreme Court brief on CEA changes.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade said on Tuesday it filed a friend-of-the-court brief last Friday in U.S. Supreme Court on behalf of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission regarding proposed changes to the Treasury Amendment of the Commodity Exchange Act (CEA).

The CBOT said the Supreme Court plans to hear the case of Dunn vs CFTC this autumn concerning the Treasury Amendment, which excludes from CEA regulation futures and options on government securities and currencies if they are traded off-exchange.

U.S. futures exchanges are seeking changes in the amendment to make regulations consistent for U.S. exchange-traded versus over-the-counter and foreign futures markets in government securities and currencies.
They say different regulation results in higher costs for exchange-traded contracts than for off-exchange products.

"Congress and the Court should not mandate that futures and options on government securities and currencies, if traded on an exchange, are subject to the CEA with its resulting costs while, if they are not exchange traded, the CEA would not apply," the CBOT said.
